newsitem.title: USA: Kevorkian drops off body after police detain him.
newsitem.headline: Kevorkian drops off body after police detain him.

text.p: Assisted suicide doctor Jack Kevorkian dropped off the body of a 55-year-old Illinois woman at a hospital emergency room on Thursday, hours after police detained him as he left a meeting with the woman.

Kevorkian brought the woman's body to William Beaumont Hospital in Royal Oak and identified her as Nancy DeSoto of Bourbonnais, Ill., near Kankakee, a hospital spokeswoman said. It was the 43rd death Kevorkian has acknowledged attending since he began his doctor-assisted suicide crusade in 1990.

Earlier Thursday, Kevorkian's lawyer, Geoffrey Fieger, said police stopped the suicide activist in the parking lot of the Dunes Motel in Royal Oak after he left a meeting with DeSoto and Janet Good, one of his associates.

DeSoto, who suffered from multiple sclerosis and was confined to a wheelchair, remained in her room at the motel. Officers later ordered the motel's manager to open the door to her room but she ordered them out because they did not have a warrant, Fieger said.
"She is a very strong woman," he added. "She refused to cooperate with them."

He also accused police of illegally tapping Kevorkian's telephone line, saying they "were at places they could only have been at if they engaged in illegal wiretapping." He added that "they were there in advance" of the meeting.

Oakland County Assistant Prosecutor Lawrence Bunting denied the allegations and said police only wanted to speak to Kevorkian. "They were probably trying to find out whether there was a dead body in the room," Bunting said.

A similar incident occured on Sept. 6 when police in nearby West Bloomfield Township broke up a meeting between Kevorkian and a patient in a hotel room. The patient, 60-year-old Isabel Correa, of Fresno, Calif., died the next day with Kevorkian's help. She suffered from a spinal cord disorder that left her bound to a wheelchair.
